in_hebrew.name: תדיה
in_hebrew.meaning: תדיה הוא שם שמשמעותו לב טוב ומושג חזק
in_hebrew.long_meaning: תדיה הוא שם עברי שמקורו ביוונית, שם שמשמעותו לב טוב ומושג חזק. השם תדיה מוזכר בברית החדשה, ומשמעותו היא שילוב של המילים 'תד' שפירושו לב ו'דיה' שפירושו טוב. השם תדיה הוא שם נפוץ בקרב הנוצרים, ומשמש כסמל לאהבה ולב טוב.

in_greek.name: Θαδδία
in_greek.meaning: Θαδδία σημαίνει καλό καρδιό και ισχυρή έννοια
in_greek.long_meaning: Θαδδία είναι ένα ελληνικό όνομα που σημαίνει καλό καρδιό και ισχυρή έννοια. Το όνομα Θαδδία αναφέρεται στη Νέα Διαθήκη, και σημαίνει συνδυασμός των λέξεων 'Θαδ' που σημαίνει καρδιά και 'δία' που σημαίνει καλό. Το όνομα Θαδδία είναι δημοφιλές μεταξύ των Χριστιανών, και χρησιμοποιείται ως σύμβολο αγάπης και καλής καρδιάς.

Today, Thaddia remains a popular name among Christians worldwide, symbolizing the values of love, kindness, and spiritual strength.

data.spiritual_significance: Thaddia holds a significant spiritual meaning, reminding us of the importance of community and loved ones in our lives. The name translates as 'my people's gift', emphasizing the idea that we are all a gift from God to our families, communities, and the world around us. Thaddia can serve as a reminder to value and cherish the relationships in our lives and to strive to be a blessing to those around us. historical_references.reference: Thaddaeus, one of the seven deacons chosen by the apostles to serve tables, is traditionally identified with the biblical figure Thaddaeus or Lebbaeus, who is mentioned as accompanying Judas Iscariot in the list of the twelve apostles. Thaddaeus is believed to have been martyred in Mesopotamia, likely during the reign of Trajan (AD 98-117).
historical_references.context: Early Christian history, Acts of the Apostles

historical_references.reference: Another tradition holds that Thaddaeus traveled to Syria and Armenia after the crucifixion and became the evangelist to those regions. He is believed to have founded the see of Edessa and is venerated as its first bishop. This tradition places Thaddaeus in the late 1st century AD.

trends: Modern usage of the Christian name 'Thaddia' is rare and usually found in religious or historical contexts. It's derived from the Aramaic name 'Levi, son of Judas' (Lee-vee thu-DAE-yah) in the New Testament. The name Thaddia is often associated with the early Christian community and saints.
